correctness.rationale: Each of the 2421 listed triples at n=17..20 is independently checked to be a distinct disconnected triple, covering all facets; Every one of the 2421 ordered facets is checked against every preceding facet and satisfies the exact local shelling criterion. The characteristic ridge-containment criterion is proved equivalent to pure shellability. Spanning counts 1,10,20,31 yield the new homotopy types; published Theorem 1.4 extends the assertion to all n>=21. Exhaustive GF(2) Alexander-dual homology for 11<=n<=16 obstructs shellability in every smaller nonvoid case. Full computation code, input orders, and recorded successful replay are embedded. Finite computations are not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the sharp p=4 shellability classification, whose new proof obligations are exact shelling orders at n=17–20. Primary full-text inspection finds only the p=2 result and a p>=2 theorem requiring n>=21 for p=4. Earlier numerical homology in Table 2 is not novel and cannot imply shellability. Search of alternative phrasings and the closest publicly indexed records found no covering theorem, subject to unindexed-work risk.
residual_risks: Possible equivalent shelling in unindexed or subsequently revised work; searches do not prove global uniqueness.
The known Table 2 includes numerical Betti values already; originality is solely the missing shellability certificates and the consequent sharp classification.

value.rationale: Completes the nontrivial fixed p=4 instance of the explicit 2025 sharp-threshold Conjecture 4.2. The exact missing shelling certificates yield a structural property beyond known integral Betti tables, with Cohen–Macaulay and integral wedge-homotopy consequences. The classification uses all four boundary n values plus an established infinite theorem; it is not an arbitrary isolated enumeration.
